rounds.text: The business is benefiting from a strong macroeconomic backdrop with Capital Goods residing in a tailwind, carrying a tailwind score of +0.68 [E50, E52]. Fundamentals are actively outpacing the stock price, as 5-year profit growth of 15% outpaces the 6% share price growth, and recent profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 123% [E38, E39]. This operational acceleration is visible in the trailing twelve months, where compounded sales growth reached 97% and compounded profit growth surged by 113% [E14, E18]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen scores the company at a neutral 60 out of 100, supported by strong metrics including YoY sales growth of 21% and YoY net profit growth of 88% [E43, E44, E46]. Promoter commitment remains rock-solid with a steady 74.00% holding, while total borrowings have successfully decreased to Rs 8.11 Cr from Rs 8.34 Cr a year prior [E31, E33]. Conceded: the company trades at a steep P/E of 584x alongside negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.10 Cr for March 2026 [E1, E28, E29].

The valuation of Thakral Services (India) Ltd is completely disconnected from economic reality, trading at an astronomical P/E ratio of 584x, which massively exceeds the sector benchmark of 23.34x [E1, E6]. This extreme multiple is compounded by an absurd EV/EBITDA of 826.44x against a sector benchmark of just 13.57x [E10]. Beneath these speculative multiples lies severe fundamental decay, highlighted by a staggering 10-year compounded sales growth of -27% and a 5-year contraction of -46% [E11, E12]. Operational efficiency is equally dismal, with the operating margin plunging to -57% in the trailing twelve months and worsening further to -82% in the June 2026 quarter [E23, E24]. Furthermore, the company is burning cash, reporting negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.10 Cr in March 2026 alongside high debtor days of 153 [E28, E29, E42]. A discounted cash flow model values the stock at a mere Rs 1 per share, reflecting a catastrophic margin of safety of -1650.0% [E35, E36]. conceded: E18

The bear's alarm over valuation multiples like the 584x P/E and 826.44x EV/EBITDA ignores the fundamental momentum currently driving an operational turnaround [E1, E6, E10, E51]. While historical sales show long-term contraction, the immediate reality is a powerful inflection point: compounded sales growth reached 97% over the trailing twelve months alongside a stellar 113% compounded profit growth [E11, E12, E14, E18]. Conceded: E23, E24, E28, E29, E35, E42. Furthermore, this positive trajectory is supported by a strong sector tailwind in Capital Goods with a tailwind score of +0.68, and fundamentals are clearly outpacing the stock where 5-year profit growth of 15% easily outstrips 6% share price growth [E16, E20, E38, E50, E52]. Promoters maintain absolute skin in the game with a steadfast 74.00% holding, and total borrowings have successfully decreased year-over-year to Rs 8.11 Cr [E31, E33]. Dismissing these active structural improvements based entirely on static DCF models overlooks how rapidly an outperforming company can re-rate when earnings grow by triple digits [E18, E35, E39, E51].

Conceded: E14, E16, E18, E31, E50, and E52. While the bull points to recent profit and sales momentum alongside sector tailwinds, these figures mask a business currently operating with negative cash flows, where operating and free cash flow stood at a concerning Rs -0.10 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E29]. The argument that triple-digit earnings growth justifies astronomical multiples ignores the company's severe structural deterioration in operating margins, which plummeted to -57% in the TTM and worsened to -82% in June 2026 [E23, E24]. Furthermore, the bull's dismissal of static valuation models overlooks a staggering reverse DCF requirement that current prices demand an unsustainable 57.6% earnings growth against a base case of 15.0%, leaving a margin of safety at -1650.0% [E35, E37]. Long-term top-line contraction of -46% over five years and exceptionally high debtors of 153 days further undermine the narrative of a stable structural turnaround [E12, E42]. Finally, returns on capital remain deeply depressed with an ROE of 0.34% and ROCE of 2.88%, trailing far behind sector benchmarks and invalidating the premise that current fundamentals support the valuation [E8, E9].
